text:
maria: Heads up — after landing the FlashAttention v2 switch in the runtime, we're seeing a tail-latency regression on long-seq chat workloads (~2-4% p95 increase). Noticed in canary traffic on Dedicated.
ajay: ugh. Any perf traces? which kernel variant picked? :eyes:
maria: I grabbed a small perf run. Root cause looks like we fall back from FA v2 fused kernel to paged attention in some batches because of our KV layout alignment. nvprof shows a spike in memcpy and kernel launches.
sasha: can you paste the profiler snippet? Also what's the KV cache layout right now (interleaved vs separate)?
maria: current layout: interleaved per-head, dtype=fp16, contiguous N, H, S, D layout. Strides make some batches unaligned to 128B. snippet:
```
# KV cache layout (simplified)
kv.shape = (batch, num_heads, seqlen, head_dim)  # contiguous
kv.strides = (num_heads*seqlen*head_dim, seqlen*head_dim, head_dim, 1)
```
ajay: here's the nvprof extract — kernel fallback and memcpy timestamps:
```
[12345ms] cuMemcpy H2D 256MB (small fragmented copies)
[12410ms] flash_attn_fused_kernel (fast) 8ms
[12418ms] paged_attention_kernel (fallback) 34ms
[12460ms] total request latency + ~28ms
```
ben: I ran microbenchmarks locally. For seqlen 2048, heads=32, head_dim=128:
- interleaved fp16 contiguous: p50 18ms, p95 40ms (paged kicked in)
- separate per-head aligned to 128B (padded): p50 16ms, p95 32ms
- bf16 vs fp16 diff ~1-2% on kernel perf but alignment had larger effect.
sasha: so layout matters more than dtype here. If some batches have different sequence lengths we create non-contiguous slices which change stride and kernel selection.
maria: exactly. Our kernel selector currently checks dtype and seqlen thresholds but doesn't inspect stride or pointer alignment. It chooses FA v2 for seqlen>256, but the kernel requires 128B alignment for the fused path.
ajay: quick idea: add an alignment check and a lightweight stride check into kernel selection. If unaligned, either re-layout the KV into an aligned buffer (memcpy cost) OR force a compatible kernel that expects separate strides.
ben: benchmarked both options:
- re-layout (single memcpy into aligned scratch) cost ~2.5ms for batch size=8,seqlen=2048 but then fused kernel runs faster and amortizes; p95 net improved ~6%.
- force paged kernel: avoids memcpy but p95 worse by ~10%.
perf-bot: [auto-bench] run_id=2026-06-18-11-02; model=gptx-large; seqlen=2048; bs=8; heads=32; hd=128; result: interleaved->paged p95=42ms, re-layout+fused p95=35ms. Details: https://ci.internal/bench/20260618/2026-06-18-11-02
sasha: given runtime constraints, re-layout only when the memcpy cost < expected kernel delta. We can estimate kernel delta from offline microbench table and do a cheap heuristic: if seqlen*head_dim*bs*bytes_per_elem > threshold then copy.
ajay: also consider alternate KV layout: separate-per-head padded to 128B on allocation so no per-request memcpy needed. Tradeoff: more memory and slightly more complex indexing.
maria: memory budget on Dedicated isn't huge for large customers, but we could make it opt-in (config flag) and default to dynamic re-layout for small batches.
ben: about strides: for CUDA kernels stride-of-last-dim==1 is required, but many of our slicing ops produce stride>1. Suggest adding a canonicalize_kv_slice helper that returns (ptr, stride_info, needs_copy).
sasha: good. Also check dtype alignment: fp16 is 2 bytes; 128B alignment means addresses should be divisible by 128 => pointer % 128 == 0. For Tensors it's often true on alloc but slicing breaks it.
ajay: implementation plan:
1) kernel_selector: add checks for pointer_alignment and contiguous_stride for the fused kernels.
2) add canonicalize_kv_slice to runtime with fast-path: if aligned+contig -> return view; else if size large -> allocate scratch + cudaMemcpyAsync + return ptr; else fallback to paged kernel.
3) add telemetry: increment metric 'kv_relayout_count' and 'kv_relayout_latency'.
maria: raising PR that wires in step 1+2 in a feature-flagged way. Will include microbench harness to verify.
ben: small note on quantization: int8 kernels change layout expectations; keep selector aware of quant dtype.
perf-bot: [alert] perf-regression-detect: p95 increase detected in canary traffic for service=inference, delta=+3.2% vs baseline. Linked thread: https://incidents.internal/PRJ-1243
maria: thanks team. I'll post the draft PR and attach the bench logs. Want to get a hotfix flag enabled for Dedicated canaries.
ajay: :thumbsup: let me know when PR ready — will review the selector logic.
sasha: also add a unit test that constructs unaligned views to ensure path correctness.
ben: and add a comment in the allocator about 128B padding for per-head separate layout.
maria: will do. Should we schedule a quick sync if the canary shows more regressions tomorrow?
ajay: yes, ping if perf-bot shows delta > 2% after the fix. :clock1:
